PullRequest.Title: Engineering - update node version in the build folder
PullRequest.Body:

Scenarios.Scenario: CI node_modules cache preparation and dependency installation across product-build platform/architecture jobs
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each job hashes dependency manifests including build/.npmrc, restores the platform-specific node_modules cache, and runs npm ci only on a cache miss before compilation can proceed.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and SHA-256 hash build/.npmrc together with package manifests and lockfiles for the node_modules cache key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per CI cache-preparation job; file count and bytes are unchanged.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same file was read and hashed with target 22.22.1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before cache restoration; the target string changes the key but not hashing cost.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Restore a node_modules cache, or fetch locked npm packages when the new key is cold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cache request per platform/architecture job; npm package fetches occur only on the first miss for each effective key and are subsequently served by the populated cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The established Node 22 key could be warm; any dependency/toolchain input change similarly created a one-time new key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A cold miss blocks dependency installation and therefore the build; warm cache restoration avoids npm ci as before.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run npm ci and native addon compilation on a cache miss.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One repository install per cold platform/architecture cache key; native build and remote installs remain sequential, with JS-only installs capped at 8.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same npm ci/native compilation path built dependencies against Node 22 on cold cache misses.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Cold installation is on the build critical path, but the diff causes only the expected one-time cache rotation and does not increase steady-state subprocess count.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One cache lookup per CI platform/architecture job; after this target change, one cold install per distinct cache-key argument set, then warm reuse for subsequent jobs/builds with unchanged inputs.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The pipeline matrix may run platform jobs concurrently. Within the repository postinstall, build and remote native installs are explicitly sequential while JS-only directory installs are capped at min(CPU count, 8); this diff does not alter either limit.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The changed build/.npmrc bytes intentionally produce a new node_modules cache key. Existing Node 22 cache entries miss once; successful Node 24 entries are then warm and reusable. There is no changed retry or negative-cache behavior.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the cache key directly includes build/.npmrc and pipeline conditions run npm ci only when restoration misses; no changed scheduling or package graph exists.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cold-install duration and number of concurrently active matrix jobs are not measured, but the cache rotation is bounded to the first successful population per effective key.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. A one-time cache miss is necessary to avoid reusing ABI-incompatible Node 22 native modules, and warm behavior is unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Developer npm install/postinstall after updating to the PR
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Preinstall compares the saved dependency state, installs node-gyp tooling and target headers when stale, then postinstall installs build native dependencies before development/build commands can use them.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hash dependency input files and compare node_modules/.postinstall-state.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per npm install/preinstall check; unchanged file count and size.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same hash included build/.npmrc containing target 22.22.1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Determines whether the near-instant fast path is used. This edit deliberately causes one stale result, then successful postinstall records the new state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: node-gyp downloads Node target headers from nodejs.org when version 24.22.1 is absent from the local header cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one cold fetch per machine/cache for the new target, coalesced by node-gyp's target-version cache; warm installs reuse it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The build target caused node-gyp to request/cache Node 22.22.1 headers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The cold header fetch blocks native compilation; it replaces the corresponding Node 22 header requirement rather than adding an additional recurring fetch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Compile the allow-listed build native addons, including tree-sitter, using the configured Node target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: The same fixed native addon graph is compiled once per stale/full install; no per-item or unbounded fan-out was added.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same native addon graph was compiled from source against Node 22.22.1.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Compilation is required before install completion. The target ABI changes, but build_from_source was already enabled and compile cardinality is unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One invalidation for an existing checkout when build/.npmrc changes; subsequent unchanged installs hit the saved postinstall state fast path. Native dependency count is fixed by build/package-lock.json.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Node header installation is synchronous. Build and remote native npm installs are sequential; other directory installs are bounded at 8. This diff changes no concurrency control.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: build/.npmrc participates in the local install-state hash, so old state becomes stale once. node-gyp stores headers under a target-version-specific cache directory; Node 24 headers are downloaded on a cold machine and reused thereafter.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: local state hashing, target-specific header caching, and install sequencing are explicit in the traced code.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Node 24 versus Node 22 header download sizes and compiler duration are not benchmarked, but there is no code evidence of increased operation count or changed scaling.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The update rotates target-specific artifacts once and preserves warm-install skipping, bounded concurrency, and native build cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Execution of build tooling that loads native build dependencies
Scenarios.CriticalPath: After dependencies are installed, build/typecheck/package tasks load native modules compiled for the running Node 24 runtime; no new runtime boundary is placed on these task paths.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Normal build inputs such as source files and bundles; the diff does not add work proportional to them.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Existing task/tool concurrency is unchanged because the edit only changes the native ABI target used at install time.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Installed native artifacts are supplied by the warmed node_modules cache or local node_modules state; the target change prevents incompatible Node 22 artifacts from being reused.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that no new filesystem, network, IPC, database, or subprocess operation is introduced on build-task execution paths.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Runtime performance differences between Node major versions are outside what this one-line ABI-target alignment establishes; no mechanism in the diff proves degradation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding. The hunk changes artifact compatibility at installation, not runtime work frequency, allocation, or boundary usage.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file diff and traced CI cache generation, cold/warm dependency installation, node-gyp header retrieval/native compilation, local install-state invalidation, and build-tool execution. The Node target update creates bounded one-time cache rotations required for ABI correctness, with unchanged warm paths, operation cardinality, and concurrency; no actionable performance regression or evidenced shipped-regression fix was found.
